title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski on Madrid atmosphere and matchup against Bengals | Press Conference
headline: Stefanski was blunt after the Madrid loss to Cincinnati, blaming self-inflicted errors and penalties in all three phases. He gave no player-specific fantasy news and no hints of lineup changes.
summary: Stefanski opened by calling the loss disappointing and not good enough. He credited Cincinnati as a well-coached team with good players, and said Atlanta had far too many self-inflicted wounds that were uncharacteristic of the team. He put the blame on offense, defense, special teams, players and coaches alike. On stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, he said you can only try to slow them down, and Atlanta didn't do enough of that. He cited schematic things to fix plus missed tackles. He called the pre-snap penalties inexcusable and said the team has to carry its practice-field sharpness into games. Asked about personnel changes, he said he reviews everything every week and gave no specifics. He declined to make proclamations about the season. He praised the Madrid trip, the fans and Real Madrid's hospitality as first class. He also said a player named James (likely Pierce) played his first game back from a long absence despite a back issue during the week, and that rust was expected. He added that the team is counting on its kicker to make his kicks.

injuries.detail: Played his first game back from a long absence after dealing with a back issue during the week. The coach expected rust and said he should be better in game two. The name was spoken in a reporter's question and is not on the provided roster.

topics.detail: Stefanski said too many uncharacteristic mistakes, especially pre-snap penalties, made the game hard to win against anyone. He wants the team to bring its practice discipline to Sundays.
He said Higgins and Chase can't be fully stopped, only slowed, and Atlanta didn't do that enough. He cited missed tackles and some schematic improvements needed, with no specific adjustments named.
Asked about changes, he said the staff evaluates what it can do better every week. He gave no sign of specific personnel moves and made no proclamations about the season.
He called the trip, the city, Real Madrid's hosting and the fans first class and outstanding, though the result was disappointing.
Stefanski said he expects the kicker to make his kicks and that the team is counting on him. He called the kicker a professional, but gave no sign of a change.

title: Dave Canales Speaks After Broncos Game
headline: Panthers drop a third straight in Denver, but Darren Waller remains Bryce Young's go-to red zone target; the OL stays under review week to week.
summary: Canales framed the loss as a clean-football problem: about 100 yards of penalties in the first half extended Denver drives, and the offense needed to be more efficient on third down. He said he mostly couldn't argue with the flags, which were for hand-fighting and contact on his corners and receivers, and he stressed technique and leverage. On the replay review, he said officials told him the challenge flag was thrown before the next snap, which took away a goal-line opportunity and turned into a Denver interception after the ball bounced off a defender's arm. He called the strip sack that ended the game a really good rush and said Carolina can help Bryce Young in that spot. He said the offensive line played generally well in the pass game, while the run game was held in check and found only some space. Line changes will be decided weekly based on who is available and the opposing front. He liked Todd Wash's aggressive defensive plan with varied personnel. He called Darren Waller exactly what the team pictured, citing the rhythm he and Young have built. His message to the team was to execute for four quarters and cut the penalties.

signals.claim: Waller will continue to be a primary red zone target for Bryce Young.
signals.note: Waller keeps finding openings against tight coverage and has a growing rhythm with Young, which supports his touchdown upside.

signals.claim: Young is developing rhythm with Waller, but the offense needs to protect him and finish drives.
signals.note: Young extended the key goal-line play, which ended in an interception, and was strip-sacked on the final drive, so late-game execution is still shaky.
signals.quote: Bryce kind of extended it and unfortunately ended in interception.

topics.detail: Carolina had about 100 penalty yards in the first half, many on corners challenging receivers outside. Canales said he mostly agreed with what the officials saw (hands, contact) and focused on technique rather than arguing the calls.
Officials confirmed the challenge flag was thrown before the snap, so the goal-line play was negated and the next play ended in a Denver interception. Canales called it a huge swing.

Canales said the group played generally well, especially in pass protection off play action, though the run game was held in check. Lineup decisions will be made weekly depending on availability and the opposing front.
Canales liked Wash's aggressive play-calling and use of different personnel, which let the defenders play fast. A few wrinkles and calls still need to be sorted out on film.
The team has lost three straight. Canales wants four quarters of consistent execution, citing assignments, finishing plays and avoiding penalties, and pointed to Denver (7-2) as the model.

title: Zac Taylor Speaks After Week 9 Victory Over Falcons in Spain | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Bengals are 6-2 on a four-game win streak: Ja'Marr Chase went for 10 catches and 150 yards, Joe Burrow is playing at a very high level, and Chase Brown and Samaje Perine both got praise before Sunday night's home game vs. Pittsburgh.
summary: Taylor was proud of the 34-17 win over Atlanta in Spain. He praised how the team handled the trip and closed out the first half, the game, and the fourth quarter, and said all three phases played well. He singled out Ja'Marr Chase for turning short completions into explosive plays, calling him the best in the world, and cited his ten catches for roughly 150 yards. He credited Chase Brown for explosive runs, said Samaje Perine also played well, and said he was pleased with the whole running back room and the offensive line. He said Joe Burrow is playing at an unbelievably high level and that it is hard not to put the ball in his hands on every play. He added that Burrow doesn't force throws and will still give Chase opportunities when defenses lean toward or double him. The defense slowed Atlanta's run game after the first quarter and produced two key turnouts late. The team is on a four-game win streak at 6-2 and turns to a big divisional home game against Pittsburgh, who already beat them once this year. No injuries were discussed.

signals.claim: Chase remains the focal point of the passing offense, and Burrow will keep giving him opportunities even against doubles.
signals.note: Chase had 10 catches for about 150 yards and is the centerpiece of the offense, so he is a locked-in WR1 with a high floor.
signals.quote: that's just Ja'Marr Chase best in the world

signals.claim: Burrow will keep being featured in the offense, with the ball in his hands on essentially every play.
signals.note: Burrow has multiple straight games with three touchdowns, and the coach says the offense runs through him, which supports a strong QB1 outlook.
signals.quote: Joe's playing an unbelievably high level right now.

signals.claim: Brown will continue to lead the backfield, getting carries and explosive runs behind the offensive line.
signals.note: He was praised for explosive runs, which supports his lead-back role even though Perine also contributed.
signals.quote: Chase Chase did a great job.

signals.claim: Perine remains a contributing part of the running back rotation.
signals.note: The coach praised his game but gave no hint of a bigger role, so he is a secondary option for now.
signals.quote: Samaje had a good game as well

topics.detail: The Bengals host Pittsburgh on Sunday night in a major divisional game. The Steelers already beat Cincinnati once this year.
After the first quarter the defense controlled Atlanta's run game, then closed out the game with two big turnovers.
Cincinnati is 6-2 and on a four-game win streak. Taylor said the team is hitting its stride but is still working to avoid repeating past mistakes.
Taylor praised the fans, the support staff, and the hosts in Madrid. He gave the game ball to equipment head Jeff Brickner and the support staff.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference at Saints: November 8th, 2026
headline: Browns lost 23-22 in overtime after Monken went for two and the try failed. Denzel Boston's ankle is a watch item, and Harold Fannin Jr. keeps producing as a checkdown and playmaker.
summary: Monken said he was proud of the team's resiliency after the 23-22 overtime loss at New Orleans. He said he went for two at the end because kicking the extra point would likely mean tying or losing, since the Saints would have two timeouts and need only a field goal. He would not describe the play and said only that it wasn't executed. He praised the quarterback who played (captioned as 'Chandler', not on the roster) for his maturity, his work ethic and his plays with his legs, after about two and a half months of mostly running scout-team cards. He declined to say whether Shedeur Sanders made a case to start, saying it was too soon after the game to get into quarterback. He said a receiver named Denzel (likely Denzel Boston) limped off, came back and made a big play. Monken said his understanding is that it's an ankle injury and that they would see how he is in the coming days. He said the team needs to start faster after six first-quarter penalties and slow starts, and he called the 4th-and-goal failure unclean up front. Harold Fannin Jr. got credit for a 39-yard play and for checking the ball down. Monken noted the team is 5-2 in one-score games, has played six of its first nine games on the road, and won't leave home again until Christmas.

injuries.detail: Limped off, then returned and made a key play. Monken's understanding is that it's an ankle, and 'we'll see how he is' once the adrenaline wears off. The identification is moderately confident, since the coach said only 'Denzel'.

signals.claim: Boston's ankle will be reassessed over the next couple of days, and his availability is not yet known.
signals.note: He was praised for toughness, but the ankle needs monitoring through the week before treating him as a safe start.
signals.quote: He's one of those real guys

signals.claim: Fannin continues to be a checkdown and short-area target who gets the ball in his hands in key situations.
signals.note: His 39-yard play and the coach's praise point to a reliable, involved role in the passing game.
signals.quote: heck of a job checking the ball down, getting the ball in his hands

signals.note: Monken wouldn't discuss the quarterback situation or whether Sanders made a case to start, so the QB job is unresolved for now.
signals.quote: I'm not getting into quarterback.

topics.detail: Monken chose to go for the win rather than kick the extra point in overtime, because the Saints would have had two timeouts and needed only a field goal. He said the try wasn't executed and didn't share the play call.

Monken praised the quarterback for his growth in work ethic, diligence and feedback to the coaches. He had taken few first-team snaps before being named starter with two weeks left to prepare. He liked the QB's plays with his legs and a third-down conversion that a holding penalty wiped out.
The early 4th-and-goal try wasn't clean from the center's back block or from the puller (Austin Barber was pulling). Monken said he still liked going for it.
The team had six first-quarter penalties, including offsides on both sides of the ball. Monken said the team has to start faster over the next eight games.
Monken said Cleveland is 5-2 in one-score games, has played six of its first nine games on the road, and plays at home for four games and a bye week before leaving again at Christmas.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: Postgame Week  9 #DALvsIND
headline: Cowboys beat the Colts 27-23 with 500+ yards; Williams went over 100 rushing, Lamb was moved into the slot, and Ferguson, Mingo and P.J. Locke all got hurt.
summary: Schottenheimer praised the team's resilience after a 27-23 win over the Colts, a week after a heartbreaking loss. He singled out the defense, especially Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark inside, with five three-and-outs, some sacks, and a game-ending interception by Caleb Downs. The offense put up over 500 yards, and he called Dak Prescott incredible. He spoke highly of Ryan Flournoy's one-handed catch and moved CeeDee Lamb into the slot to test the Colts. Lamb had almost 200 yards but lost a fumble that was ruled a turnover because the ball was dislodged at the wrist rather than the forearm. The coach also admitted the team needs to clean up untimely penalties and turnovers. For injuries, he said a knee issue should be okay, Jake Ferguson had a stinger and then a knee problem, Jonathan Mingo hurt an ankle, and P.J. Locke had another concussion. Several unnamed players, including a corner with a foot problem and a player with a hamstring issue, tried to play but ran out of time, and he hopes to have them back this week. Cobie Durant and DaRon Bland stepped in at corner, and prep for San Francisco starts Monday.

injuries.detail: Had a stinger, then a knee issue, during the game. No timeline given.
Hurt an ankle early on third down and tried to play through it.
Suffered another concussion. The coach said the team is keeping him in prayers and gave no timeline.

signals.claim: Williams will remain a key part of a RB one-two punch after rushing for over 100 yards.
signals.note: He topped 100 yards after a slow start, which keeps him a strong RB option heading into the San Francisco game.
signals.quote: Javonte getting over 100 yards a day was really cool.

signals.claim: Lamb will keep moving between outside and the slot, with shots designed for him.
signals.note: He had nearly 200 yards, and the coach shrugged off the costly fumble as a competitor's mistake.

He and Williams dominated inside and drove the pass rush and run defense.

Several players who were uncertain Friday and Saturday could not go. One corner has a foot and ankle problem, and another player has a hamstring problem. The coach hopes to get them back this week. Some kicking-unit injury news was mentioned, with more imaging planned for Monday.
Lamb's fumble was ruled a turnover under the wrist-versus-forearm rule. The coach credited the defense for stopping the Colts on the next drive, limiting them to a field goal.

title: Campbell on Week 9 performance
headline: Lions win No. 6 behind a dominant front: McNeill is playing the best ball of his career. Miles Frazier got the nod over Christian Mahogany on a team-rules decision, and Frazier's job isn't locked in.
summary: Dan Campbell opened by saying the Lions got win number six, though they created some of their own issues and have things to clean up. He praised the defense and said the offense hit explosive plays when it needed them. He said the week was emotionally hard because of Jack Campbell's situation, and that the team prepared and played with him in mind. He said the team is improving through trust and execution, and that the defensive front is shutting down the run and, in the second half, getting to the quarterback. He singled out Alim McNeill as playing the best football he has seen from him, called Hutchinson a player who demands extra attention from opponents, and credited Derrick Moore, Skyler Gill-Howard and Tyleik Williams for their effort. He explained that Miles Frazier got his opportunity over Christian Mahogany because of team rules, and warned it doesn't necessarily stay that way. He admitted the offensive line struggled with protection early, getting beaten on the edge, before tightening up in the second half. He also took the blame for a special-teams decision around a DeAndre Carter return that Miami exploited, saying he should have played it safe.

injuries.detail: Coach gave no specifics but said Jack is improving and getting better every day. The team is keeping a locker set up for him that travels with them.

signals.claim: Frazier got the opportunity over Mahogany this week, but it may not remain that way going forward.
signals.note: A short-term opening on the offensive line, but Campbell explicitly said the arrangement could change.
signals.quote: Miles deserved his opportunity, and so he got it.

signals.claim: Mahogany lost his spot for this game because of team rules.
signals.note: The setback appears disciplinary rather than performance-related, so his return to the lineup is uncertain.
signals.quote: team rules

signals.claim: McNeill will keep winning one-on-ones and generating interior pressure.
signals.note: Campbell says he is playing the best football of his career, which is a boost for IDP value.
signals.quote: He's playing the best football I've ever seen him play.

signals.claim: Hutchinson continues to draw heavy opposing resources, which creates one-on-ones for teammates.
signals.note: His steady, high-level play keeps his IDP value strong while others benefit from the attention he commands.
signals.quote: Hutch is Hutch.

signals.claim: Moore is contributing as part of the pass-rush rotation.
signals.note: Campbell says he won his matchups, so he is a pass-rush name to monitor for IDP.
signals.quote: D Moore won today.

signals.claim: Gill-Howard showed strong effort, including chasing down the quarterback.
signals.note: Positive effort praise points to a growing rotation role on the line.
signals.quote: I was so impressed with running the quarterback down

signals.claim: Williams contributed to the pass rush and run defense.
signals.note: Part of the effective interior rotation, with positive comments from Campbell.
signals.quote: Ty did it.

signals.claim: Clark is a reliable veteran presence in the safety group after making a big interception.
signals.note: His turnover and the coach's trust support his role in the secondary.
signals.quote: Chuck's a rock for us back there.

signals.claim: Jack Campbell continues to improve day by day.
signals.note: His availability and status remain unclear, so monitor future updates.
signals.quote: he is improving, he's getting better every day

topics.detail: The week was emotionally difficult because of Jack Campbell's situation. The team prepared and played to honor him, and Campbell credited the leadership in the locker room.
Opposing rushers got open early and beat the Lions on the edge. Protection improved in the second half after adjustments.
The front shut down the run and got home late. The secondary rotation used everyone, and the first-half pass rush improved after halftime.
Campbell said he should have gone safe on a decision involving a DeAndre Carter return, and took the blame.
Campbell said they use every defensive back in the rotation and named Rakestraw, McCreary and Abney among those contributing.

title: Shane Steichen: Colts vs. Cowboys postgame
headline: Colts blew a 27-23 loss to Dallas with Jonathan Taylor's role under trade speculation (the coach refused to address it) and Josh Downs' day clouded by trade-request talk; Carlies, Travis and Alie-Cox all left hurt.
summary: Steichen opened by listing injuries: Jaylon Carlies (neck), Jalen Travis (knee) and Mo Alie-Cox (groin). He said the team prepared well and fought, but Dallas made more plays late. He blamed execution: a turnover, drops, explosive plays allowed, and a third-and-8 that wasn't converted when the Colts could have bled the clock. He said the offense needs better scheming to get receivers open in the vertical game, and that this starts with him. On the run game, he praised Jalen Farmer, in his second game playing, and Seth McGowan, and said the team topped 100 rushing yards with some explosives. Asked why Jonathan Taylor has been less involved for two straight games, he said there was no reason beyond game flow, pointing to four consecutive three-and-outs. He wouldn't discuss trade speculation about Taylor or whether the roster will look different after Tuesday, and he admitted the trade talk is a real thing that may affect some players more than others. He defended Josh Downs, saying he had a great week of practice and was engaged, even though Downs had a few plays he'd want back.

injuries.detail: Neck injury suffered in the game; no further timeline given.
Groin injury suffered during the game; no timeline given.

signals.note: Steichen would not say Taylor will be on the roster past Tuesday's deadline, so his situation is a real fantasy risk.
signals.quote: I'm not going to get into any trade speculations. He's on our football team.

signals.claim: Taylor's smaller recent workload was due to game flow, not a deliberate decision.
signals.note: The coach denied any intentional cutback, but two straight light games is a concern until the volume returns.
signals.quote: No, there was no reason behind that. Just the way the game played out.

signals.claim: Downs was fully engaged in practice despite the trade-request talk.
signals.note: Steichen defended Downs after some mistakes, but his trade situation hangs over his outlook.
signals.quote: I thought he had a great week of practice, I really did.

signals.claim: McGowan is a contributor in the run game.
signals.note: He earned praise as the Colts topped 100 rushing yards, which helps his share of the backfield work.
signals.quote: Seth ran hard today.

signals.claim: Farmer is playing in the lineup and has played two games so far.
signals.note: His play matters for run-game efficiency, which affects the backfield's fantasy outlook.
signals.quote: farm stepped up and did some good things.

signals.note: His hustle forced a fumble that gave the offense the ball back, a positive for IDP managers.
signals.quote: it was phenomenal.

topics.detail: Steichen cited a turnover, drops and explosive plays allowed. He said the team needs to practice more end-of-game and two-minute situations, and that he must coach better.
He said the vertical passing game needs better scheming to get receivers open, and that it starts with him.
CeeDee Lamb had a huge game and the Colts couldn't limit him. Steichen said the first touchdown may have involved a coverage miscommunication that he would review.
Steichen said trade talk is real and may affect some players more than others. He said the team has until Tuesday and then it's done, and he wouldn't say whether the roster will look different.
The Colts let Dallas score from the one-yard line to get the ball back, and a long field goal attempt was moved after a back-and-forth with the officials.

title: Coach John Harbaugh: 'It’s a huge win for us'
headline: J.J. McCarthy gutted out an injury in the win over Philly and now has to get healthy for Thursday night. Jameis Winston is the fallback, and rookie Arvell Reese was the defensive star.
summary: Harbaugh called the win over the Eagles a huge one. It ended a long losing streak in Philadelphia, which he said had been 'hovering' over the team. He praised the defense and the kick and punt coverage, and he liked that the team played smart, avoided big plays, and did not turn the ball over. J.J. McCarthy was hurt in the game, went to the locker room, and then insisted on returning. He was even allowed to stay in on the final drive after the staff considered another QB, and he is described as 'in pain.' Harbaugh said McCarthy will have to fight to be ready for the Thursday night game at MetLife. Jameis Winston filled in well, and Harbaugh singled out his deep sideline throw to Malachi Fields as the throw of the game. Rookie Arvell Reese earned the first defensive game ball for a huge stat line, with tackles, tackles for loss, sacks and pressures. On the trade deadline, Harbaugh said no one on the roster is being shopped and the team won't overpay for a short-term fix. The front office is making lots of calls, and he called nothing imminent while ruling nothing out. He was pleased with the kicker, Zavala, on difficult windy kicks.

injuries.detail: Was hurt in the game and was in pain, but returned and insisted on playing through the final drive. Harbaugh said he must fight to be ready for Thursday night.

signals.claim: McCarthy's availability for Thursday night's game is uncertain and depends on his recovery.
signals.note: A short week with an injured starting QB makes his status a key item to monitor before Thursday's lineup lock.
signals.quote: Now he's going to have to fight to get ready to play on Thursday.

signals.claim: Winston is the backup ready to play if McCarthy can't go on Thursday.
signals.note: He performed well in relief and would be the next-man-up QB, which boosts the Giants' passing game if McCarthy is limited.
signals.quote: you got to give Jameis a lot of credit

signals.claim: Fields was the target on the key deep sideline completion that started a scoring drive.
signals.note: He showed he can win downfield and could earn more targets.
signals.quote: Malachi runs a great route.

signals.claim: Reese is a game-changing rookie defender who will keep playing a major role.
signals.note: His tackles, TFLs, sacks and pressures make him a rising IDP option.
signals.quote: He had TFLs. He had sacks. He had pressures.

topics.detail: Harbaugh said there is nobody on the roster the Giants want to trade, and no one has emerged they want to trade for. They won't pay an exorbitant price for a short-term fix, but will do a deal that makes sense short and long term. They are making a lot of calls.

Asked about a reported offer to the Colts for Taylor, he said the conversations are happening and positions change daily. He did not deny the report, said nothing is ruled out, and said nothing looks imminent.
Harbaugh said Zavala made difficult kicks in the Philadelphia wind and showed what the team believes he is capable of.
The team played winning football in all three phases, led by the defense, with good coverage units and no turnovers or big plays allowed. The win ends a long losing streak against Philadelphia.

title: HC Aaron Glenn Postgame Press Conference (11/8) | Week 9
headline: Jets fall to 2-7 after a second-half collapse; Omar Cooper Jr. left late but is expected to be okay, Geno Smith was hit repeatedly, and David Bailey is a growing disruptive force.
summary: Aaron Glenn called the game a tale of two halves: the Jets hit their keys to victory in the first half, then faded after halftime. Offensively they didn't get enough possessions, and defensively they couldn't stop the run in the second half once Kenneth Walker got going. He repeatedly took the blame for red-zone failures, saying the Jets settled for field goals when they needed touchdowns against a team like Kansas City. He said Omar Cooper Jr. came out late but he believes he's okay, and that the team had no other injuries. Glenn praised Geno Smith's early play and his checks in the running game, but said Kansas City's pressure turned up and Smith was hit too often, a problem the team has to fix. He downplayed Smith's visible frustration as competitiveness. Glenn also said David Bailey, back in the lineup, is learning and improving every game, and the Jets expect him to be on the field as much as possible. He said he'd spend a lot of time thinking about how to get the team to play two complete halves.

injuries.detail: Came out of the game late; Glenn said he thinks Cooper is okay, though he was not sure of the exact issue and floated a possible sprained ankle. No other injuries reported.

signals.claim: The Jets will work to cut down how often Smith gets hit after the heavy pressure from Kansas City.
signals.note: Pass protection problems and heavy pressure could limit Smith's efficiency and the passing offense, though Glenn says he has been playing at a high level.

signals.claim: Bailey will be on the field as much as possible going forward.
signals.note: A growing snap share and disruptive plays, including a forced fumble, boost his IDP value as a pass rusher.

signals.claim: Cooper, who left the game late, is expected to be okay.
signals.note: The injury is minor by Glenn's account, but check his practice status early in the week.
signals.quote: I know Omar came out late. Um, but I think he's okay.

topics.detail: The Jets were strong in the first half but fell off after halftime, with fewer offensive possessions and a run defense that wore down. Glenn said he must think long and hard about how to prevent lulls.
The Jets settled for field goals, including after two takeaways, and Glenn stressed they need touchdowns. He said the concepts and execution have to be right, and that it falls on him.
Asked why Kenneth Walker was left wide open on a touchdown catch, Glenn said he needs to make a better call to help the players.
At 2-7, Glenn said belief comes from the process and from film of the strong first half and the offense's high level over the last two weeks.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: November 8, 2026
headline: Eagles offense is broken after a 19-11 loss to the Giants. Joe Milton got a mostly positive review as QB, but Sirianni wouldn't commit to any changes and the team heads into the bye reviewing everything.
summary: Sirianni opened by saying he talked to players after the loss to the Giants, which is why the press conference started late. He called Joe Milton's performance a mix of good plays and ones he'd want back, praising his work with his feet, the shot chances downfield, and the play-action game. He said the offense needs better complementary football so the run game can pair with play action. He defended the fourth-and-one call even though it failed. He declined to assign blame for the unblocked sack-fumble, saying it was both coaching and execution, and he took responsibility himself. He blamed the stalled run game on several things: a holding penalty on a zone-read run to open the second half, a third-down conversion rate around 20%, and too few plays. He said he wouldn't change just for the sake of changing, though everything is on the table, and the bye week will be used to look at simplifying the offense, the scheme, and staffing without committing to anything. He took the blame for the offense not being good enough, said the defense and special teams have been solid, and said the offensive failures belong to everyone. He also gave credit to Giants defensive coordinator Shane Bowen's counter to their protection calls, which he said he would review.

signals.claim: Milton remains the Eagles' quarterback and will be evaluated on film, with no sign of a change.
signals.note: Sirianni was mostly positive about Milton, but the offense's overall dysfunction caps his fantasy outlook until the bye-week fixes show up.

topics.detail: Sirianni said the offense needs to be figured out and took responsibility. He cited poor third-down efficiency (about 20%) and a lack of plays as reasons the run game never got going.
He was fine with the call despite the failure. The team had plenty of time to debate it because of the two-minute warning, and he said they'd go back to the drawing board.
On the unblocked sack-fumble, Sirianni said it was both coaching and execution, and he would not assign blame to a person or to the new quarterback. Corrections will be made in person.
The team will look at everything during the bye, including simplifying the offense and the scheme, but he said he doesn't believe in changing just to change. He did not commit to any staff changes.
He called the defense solid and said special teams have been good, with room for more consistency.

opponent: New York Giants (Week 9 result, a 19-11 loss)
